title: Popular Forms
intro: Blues, jazz standards and pop songs have their own forms: the 12-bar blues, the 32-bar AABA song and the verse–chorus song. Each is a fixed frame that players and listeners know by heart.

blocks.text: Twelve bars in three four-bar lines, each a call and response:

items: Bars 1–4: I I I I (or I IV I I, the 'quick change'). Lyrics: line 1.
Bars 5–8: IV IV I I. Lyrics: line 1 repeated.
Bars 9–12: V IV I V (or V IV I I, with V as a 'turnaround' to start the next chorus). Lyrics: the answering line.

blocks.text: All three chords are usually dominant sevenths (C7, F7, G7 in C), which no common-practice rule allows for a tonic, and the melody uses the blues scale over them; the clash of minor-third melody against major-third chord is the blues sound. Jazz blues adds secondary dominants and ii–Vs, one bar each: | C7 | F7 | C7 | Gm7 C7 | F7 | F♯°7 | C7 | A7 | Dm7 | G7 | C7 A7 | Dm7 G7 |.

blocks.text: The form of most Tin Pan Alley and Broadway songs and therefore of most jazz standards: four eight-bar sections, A A B A. The B section, the bridge (or 'release'), contrasts in key and melody. 'Over the Rainbow', 'I Got Rhythm' and 'Blue Moon' are AABA. Jazz musicians improvise over repeated choruses of the form.

Rock and pop since the 1960s: verses (same music, new words) alternate with a chorus (same words and music each time, the 'hook'). Typical layout: intro, verse, (pre-chorus), chorus, verse, chorus, bridge, chorus, outro. The chorus is usually the most energetic, often harmonically more stable and higher in register.

Pop harmony shares tonal harmony's chords but not all its habits. Corpus studies of rock (de Clercq and Temperley 2011) find IV and ♭VII far more common than in classical music, frequent retrogressions such as V–IV, and loops of four chords repeated through a section (vi–IV–I–V, I–V–vi–IV). Function is carried more by the loop and the melody than by cadences.

blocks.title: Bars
blocks.text: How many bars is one chorus of an AABA tune with 8-bar sections, and where does the bridge start?
solution: 4 × 8 = 32 bars. The bridge (B) is the third section, starting at bar 17.
